_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'Grade 10-12 Geography Syllabus' (2013, published by CDC), Section A (Map Work) and Section B (Elements of Physical Geography), covering Topics 10.1-10.8 (all of Grade 10 Sections A and B). Topic/sub-topic names and Specific Outcome statements only — the 'Content' (Knowledge/Skills/Values) columns are omitted throughout because the source PDF's table has 6 columns and text-extracts with columns interleaved out of order, risking misattribution of content between sub-topics if reconstructed automatically; the numbered Specific Outcomes, by contrast, were manually traced against each sub-topic heading in the raw extraction (verifying block order and outcome count per sub-topic) and are reproduced reliably, not guessed or sourced externally. Two numbering slips were found in the source document itself (not extraction artifacts) and corrected here based on the outcome's actual position under its sub-topic heading rather than its printed code: (1) sub-topics 10.2.6 and 10.2.7 both carry the printed code prefix '10.2.7.x' — their outcome statements are included without that ambiguous code; (2) the six Specific Outcomes belonging under sub-topics 10.5.1 (River Systems and Drainage Patterns) and 10.5.2 (River Erosion, Transportation and Deposition) are printed with the code prefix '10.8.1.x', which is also the prefix used for the five outcomes actually under Topic 10.8 (Natural Environmental Hazards) — the river outcomes have been renumbered here as 10.5.1.x/10.5.2.x to match their true topic, and the 10.8.1.x outcomes retained are the five that are actually about natural hazards. Grade 11 and 12 (Sections C and D, and beyond) are not yet included. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 10 is modeled as a single term here.

curriculum.name: 2013 Outcome-Based Curriculum
curriculum.description: Zambia's 2013 outcome-based curriculum for Grades 10-12 (Senior Secondary).

subject.name: Geography
subject.description: Senior Secondary Geography syllabus, Grade 10-12 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2013).

terms.name: Year (not term-divided in the source syllabus)

topics.name: 10.1 Map Work: Basic Techniques and Skills

competencies.description: Match conventional signs with ground features
Measure real distances between objects in the field
Translate map distances into real distances
Compute the gradient (slope) between two features on the map
Identify relief features and drainage patterns using contour lines on a map
Identify factors which influence human settlements and activities on a map
Identify vegetation and land-use types
Account for observed vegetation and land use patterns
Identify and present variables on a graphical axis
Draw a sketch map from topographic maps
Draw a cross-section between two points on a map

topics.name: 10.2 The Solar System
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

competencies.description: Describe the solar system
Describe the shape of the Earth
Explain latitude and longitude
Locate places on the Earth's surface using latitudes and longitudes
Calculate distances using latitudes
Calculate local time using longitudes
Calculate longitude from local time
Explain the International Date Line
Calculate time and date east or west of the International Date Line

sub_topics.name: 10.2.6 Apparent Movement of the Sun (Angle of Elevation)

competencies.description: Calculate the position of the midday sun (angle of elevation) at a given latitude at different times of the year
Calculate the latitude of a place using the position of the midday sun (angle of elevation)

sub_topics.name: 10.2.7 Rotation and Revolution of the Earth

competencies.description: Explain the effects of rotation of the earth
Explain the effects of the earth's revolution

topics.name: 10.3 Earth Movements
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

competencies.description: Distinguish forces leading to faulting and folding
Explain the landforms resulting from faulting and folding
Describe the distribution of landforms resulting from faulting and folding
Explain the origins of earthquakes and volcanoes
Describe the types of volcanoes
Discuss the various landforms resulting from volcanic activities
Explain effects of earthquakes and volcanic activities on the environment and people
Describe the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes

topics.name: 10.4 Weathering and Mass Wasting
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

sub_topics.name: 10.4.1 Weathering in the Tropics and Temperate Regions

competencies.description: Explain the processes of weathering
Describe the agents of weathering
Discuss the processes of mass movement or mass wasting

topics.name: 10.5 River Processes
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

competencies.description: Describe river systems
Identify river drainage patterns
Explain the stages in the formation of a river
Describe the features associated with each stage of a river
Describe processes of river erosion, transportation and deposition
Explain erosional and depositional features
Discuss the importance of rivers

topics.name: 10.6 Weather and Climate
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

competencies.description: Describe formation, structure and effects of Tropical and Temperate storms
Locate on a world map major climatic types
Describe the characteristics of climatic types

topics.name: 10.7 Vegetation
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

competencies.description: Explain the characteristics of natural vegetation (adaptation)

topics.name: 10.8 Natural Environmental Hazards
topics.description: Section B: Elements of Physical Geography.

competencies.description: Describe the natural environmental hazards
Explain the impact of human activities on the physical environment
Describe effects of hazards on people and the environment
Suggest possible solutions to natural environmental hazards
Assess the impact of climate change on the environment
